renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: plddt_by_engine
  title: Residue confidence along the sequence
  description: |-
    Each curve is the per-residue pLDDT of the top-ranked structure of one engine for one target, with chains of a complex drawn separately. It answers which regions of the sequence an engine places confidently.
    How to read: stretches above 90 are very high confidence, 70 to 90 confident, 50 to 70 low and below 50 very low, which often marks intrinsically disordered regions. Dips between confident stretches usually separate domains or flexible linkers. When engines disagree on a region, treat its placement as unreliable.
    Note: the bands are AlphaFold DB's reading guide and are not drawn on the plot. Curves longer than 200 residues are averaged over windows by this catalog's recipe, a display limit and not an engine setting.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34791371/ and https://www.ebi.ac.uk/training/online/courses/alphafold/inputs-and-outputs/evaluating-alphafolds-predicted-structures-using-confidence-scores/plddt-understanding-local-confidence/
  kind: profile
  config:
    x_title: Residue position
    y_title: pLDDT
    legend_pos: bottom
    residue_axis: true
  roles:
    series: series
    x: position
    y: plddt

- component: figure
  id: plddt_box
  title: Residue confidence per curve
  description: |-
    Each box is the spread of per-residue pLDDT over one curve of the profile tile, so one box per target and engine. It answers which engine gives the most confident structure overall.
    How to read: a box high up with a short range means a uniformly confident structure, and a long lower whisker means disordered or poorly placed regions. Compare boxes of the same target across engines, and open the profile to see where the low values sit.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median residue pLDDT of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of proteinfold.
  visu_type: box
  dict_kwargs:
    x: series
    y: plddt
    color: series
    labels:
      series: Target and engine
      plddt: pLDDT
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: plddt

- component: table
  title: Residue confidence per engine
  description: |-
    One row per residue and curve with its pLDDT.
    How to read: sort by pLDDT to list the least confident residues of a target.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: plddt_vs_ptm
  title: Local against global confidence
  description: |-
    Each point is a predicted model: its mean pLDDT on the horizontal axis and its predicted TM score on the vertical axis, coloured by engine and sized by the number of residues. It answers whether a model is trustworthy locally and as a whole.
    How to read: models in the upper right are confident on both counts. A high pLDDT with a low pTM means well folded pieces that are badly arranged, and the lower left holds models that are probably wrong. Engines that write no pTM are not drawn.
    Lines and annotations: the vertical line is a mean pLDDT of 70, the AlphaFold DB threshold for a confident residue. The horizontal line is a pTM of 0.5, above which the overall fold of the model might be similar to the true structure.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34791371/ and https://www.ebi.ac.uk/training/online/courses/alphafold/inputs-and-outputs/evaluating-alphafolds-predicted-structures-using-confidence-scores/confidence-scores-in-alphafold-multimer/
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Mean pLDDT
    y_title: pTM
    top_n_labels: 5
    legend_pos: bottom
    quadrants:
      x: 70
      y: 0.5
      labels:
      - Weak locally, fold likely
      - Confident
      - Likely wrong
      - Placed well, fold doubtful
  roles:
    x: mean_plddt
    y: ptm
    label: model_id
    color: engine
    size: n_residues

- component: card
  id: model_plddt
  title: Model confidence
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median over models of the mean pLDDT, and the strip counts models by band. It answers how confident the predictions are overall.
    How to read: models at or above 70 are confident on average, those between 50 and 70 are low and those below 50 are very low. The minimum and maximum show the range across models.
    Lines and annotations: the cut-offs are 70 and 50, the AlphaFold DB confidence bands for pLDDT.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34791371/
  column: mean_plddt
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: threshold
  threshold_value: 70.0
  threshold_direction: min
  threshold_warn: 50.0
  caption: models by mean pLDDT band
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: model_confident_share
  title: Confidently placed residues
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median percentage of a model's residues at pLDDT 70 or more, and the box shows its spread. It answers how much of a typical model is placed confidently.
    How to read: a high share with a tight box means whole models are reliable. A low or wide box means disordered proteins or hard targets, so check which engine and target sit low.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34791371/
  column: confident_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median share, with its spread

- component: card
  id: model_ptm
  title: Predicted TM score
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median pTM over models that report one, and the strip counts models above and below 0.5. It answers how many predicted folds are likely to match the real one.
    How to read: a pTM above 0.5 means the overall predicted fold might be similar to the true structure, and below 0.5 the model is likely wrong. Engines that write no pTM are left out.
    Lines and annotations: the cut-off is 0.5, from the EMBL-EBI AlphaFold course.
    Source: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/training/online/courses/alphafold/inputs-and-outputs/evaluating-alphafolds-predicted-structures-using-confidence-scores/confidence-scores-in-alphafold-multimer/
  column: ptm
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: threshold
  threshold_value: 0.5
  threshold_direction: min
  caption: models by pTM at the 0.5 floor

- component: card
  id: model_iptm
  title: Interface confidence
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median ipTM over complexes, and the strip counts models by band. It answers how well the subunits of a complex are placed against each other.
    How to read: values above 0.8 are confident high-quality predictions, values between 0.6 and 0.8 are uncertain and values below 0.6 suggest a failed prediction. Single chains have no ipTM and are not counted.
    Lines and annotations: the cut-offs are 0.8 and 0.6, from the EMBL-EBI AlphaFold course.
    Source: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/training/online/courses/alphafold/inputs-and-outputs/evaluating-alphafolds-predicted-structures-using-confidence-scores/confidence-scores-in-alphafold-multimer/
  column: iptm
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - max
  secondary_layout: threshold
  threshold_value: 0.8
  threshold_direction: min
  threshold_warn: 0.6
  caption: complexes by ipTM band

- component: card
  id: model_count
  title: Predicted models
  description: |-
    The hero number is the number of predicted models in view, the bars rank the engines by how many they wrote, and the line below gives the highest rank. It answers how many models each engine produced.
    How to read: engines write a different number of models per target. A short bar usually means an engine that returns a single model.
  column: model_rank
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: engine
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: models, by engine

- component: figure
  id: engine_box
  title: Model confidence per engine
  description: |-
    Each box is the spread of the mean pLDDT of an engine's models. It answers which engine gives the most confident predictions on these targets.
    How to read: a higher box means more confident models, but confidence is not accuracy, so a high box from an engine that disagrees with the others deserves a second look. Compare the same targets across engines before preferring one.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median mean pLDDT of a model of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of proteinfold.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34791371/
  visu_type: box
  dict_kwargs:
    x: engine
    y: mean_plddt
    color: engine
    labels:
      engine: Engine
      mean_plddt: Mean pLDDT
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: mean_plddt

- component: figure
  id: rank_line
  title: Confidence by model rank
  description: |-
    Each line follows the mean pLDDT of the models of one engine and target from the top-ranked one downwards. It answers how much worse the lower-ranked models are.
    How to read: a flat line means the models agree and the ranking hardly matters. A steep fall means only the top models are worth using.
  visu_type: line
  dict_kwargs:
    x: model_rank
    y: mean_plddt
    color: structure
    labels:
      model_rank: Model rank
      mean_plddt: Mean pLDDT
      structure: Engine and target

- component: interactive
  title: Engine
  description: Keep the models of one or more engines.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: engine

- component: interactive
  title: Model rank
  description: Restrict the tiles to a range of model ranks, where rank 1 is the top-ranked model.
  interactive_type: RangeSlider
  column_name: model_rank

- component: table
  title: Model confidence scores
  description: |-
    One row per predicted model with its rank, mean pLDDT, confident and very low shares and the pTM, ipTM and ipSAE scores. Selecting rows filters the tab to them.
    How to read: sort by pTM or ipTM to list the models most and least likely to be correct.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: model_id

outputs.name: Multiple sequence alignments of the MSA-based engines

renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: folding_msa
  title: Alignment behind the fold
  description: |-
    Each row is a homologous sequence aligned to the query, which comes first, with residues coloured by type. It answers how much evolutionary evidence the engine had for each position.
    How to read: columns that stay the same in every row are conserved, and gap-filled stretches mean few homologues cover that region. A shallow or low-identity alignment predicts a less reliable structure, so compare it with the confidence tiles. Brushing columns selects those residues on the structure.
    Note: this catalog's recipe keeps at most 500 rows per alignment, a display limit and not a limit of the engine's search.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/proteinfold/master/docs/output.md
  kind: msa
  roles:
    msa_id: msa_id
    seq_id: seq_id
    sequence: aligned_sequence
    rank: rank
    identity: identity

- component: card
  id: msa_depth
  title: Alignment depth
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median number of sequences in the alignment of a target, and the box shows its spread. It answers how many homologues the engine could draw on.
    How to read: deep alignments give the engine more co-evolution signal. Targets with very few sequences are hard cases whose confidence scores deserve caution.
    Note: depth counts the stored rows, which are capped at 500.
  column: depth
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median depth, with its spread

- component: card
  id: msa_coverage
  title: Query coverage
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of the query covered by an aligned sequence, and the box shows its spread. It answers whether homologues span the whole query or only a part.
    How to read: coverage near full length means global homologues. Low coverage means the hits match a single domain, so the rest of the protein is predicted without evidence.
  column: coverage
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median coverage, with its spread

- component: figure
  id: identity_histogram
  title: Sequence identity to the query
  description: |-
    Each bar counts aligned sequences in an identity bin against the query, coloured by engine. It answers how close the homologues are to the target.
    How to read: a mass of high identities means close relatives, and a spread towards low identities means distant homologues that carry the evolutionary signal. A histogram piled at the low end means the alignment adds little.
  visu_type: histogram
  dict_kwargs:
    x: identity
    color: engine
    labels:
      identity: Identity to the query
      engine: Engine

- component: table
  title: Aligned sequences
  description: |-
    One row per aligned sequence with its identity and coverage against the query.
    How to read: sort by identity to find the closest and most distant homologues.

outputs.name: Predicted aligned error of the top-ranked models

renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: pae_heatmap
  title: Predicted aligned error
  description: |-
    Each cell is the predicted aligned error, in Angstrom, between a row of residues and a column of residues of the top-ranked model, averaged into bins. It answers how confidently two regions of the structure are placed relative to each other.
    How to read: low values off the diagonal mean two domains, or two chains, are confidently positioned. High values mean their relative position is uncertain even if each domain is well folded. Rows are annotated by engine.
    Note: the error is capped at 31.75 Angstrom by AlphaFold, and no cut-off grades it, so no line is drawn.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34791371/
  kind: complex_heatmap
  roles:
    index: residue_range
    row_annotation_cols:
    - engine

- component: card
  id: mean_pae
  title: Mean predicted error
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean predicted aligned error over the matrix, and the box shows the spread of the row means. It answers how well placed the structure is overall.
    How to read: lower is better. A low mean with a few high rows points to one badly placed region, so open the matrix to find it.
  column: mean_pae
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: mean error, with its spread

- component: interactive
  title: Engine
  description: Show the matrices of one engine.
  interactive_type: Select
  column_name: engine

- component: table
  title: Predicted aligned error bins
  description: |-
    One row per residue bin with its mean error and the error against every other bin.
    How to read: sort by mean error to find the bins that are least well placed.

outputs.name: Residue confidence of each engine's models

renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: plddt_model_spread
  title: Confidence across models
  description: |-
    Each curve is the per-residue pLDDT of the top-ranked model of one engine, with a band from the lowest to the highest model at that residue. It answers where an engine's models agree and where they do not.
    How to read: a narrow band means every model places the residue alike. A wide band marks regions the engine is unsure about, and curves that part mark regions where engines disagree. Above 90 is very high confidence, 70 to 90 confident, 50 to 70 low and below 50 very low.
    Note: the bands of pLDDT are AlphaFold DB's reading guide and are not drawn on the plot. Residues are counted from 1 over the chains in order.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34791371/
  kind: profile
  config:
    x_title: Residue position
    y_title: pLDDT
    legend_pos: bottom
    residue_axis: true
  roles:
    series: engine
    x: residue_index
    y: plddt
    lower: plddt_min
    upper: plddt_max

- component: interactive
  title: Target
  description: Show one target at a time, so the curves of its engines are comparable.
  interactive_type: Select
  column_name: target

- component: table
  title: Confidence across models
  description: |-
    One row per residue and engine with the top-ranked pLDDT and the lowest and highest value across models.
    How to read: sort by the gap between lowest and highest to find unstable residues.

outputs.name: Residue confidence of the top-ranked structures

renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: structure_plddt
  title: Structure coloured by confidence
  description: |-
    Each atom of the top-ranked structure is coloured by the pLDDT of its residue, in the four AlphaFold DB confidence bands. It answers which parts of the fold can be trusted.
    How to read: regions in the two upper bands are reliable. Well folded cores usually sit there, while loops, termini and disordered regions fall in the two lower bands. Interpret the arrangement of the low bands with caution.
    Lines and annotations: the bands are pLDDT above 90 (very high), 70 to 90 (confident), 50 to 70 (low) and below 50 (very low), as used by AlphaFold DB.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34791371/
  kind: molecule_3d
  roles:
    position: position
    entity: entity
    chain: chain
    value: value
    category: category

- component: advanced_viz
  id: plddt_sequence_track
  title: Confidence along the sequence
  description: |-
    Each cell is one residue of the sequence, with its amino acid and a lane coloured by its pLDDT. It answers which stretches of the sequence are confidently predicted.
    How to read: continuous high stretches are well predicted domains, and runs of low values are flexible or disordered segments. Selecting a residue highlights it on the structure.
    Lines and annotations: the lane uses the AlphaFold DB bands, above 90 very high, 70 to 90 confident, 50 to 70 low and below 50 very low.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34791371/
  kind: sequence_track
  config:
    value_label: pLDDT
  roles:
    position: position
    entity: entity
    residue: residue
    value: value

- component: card
  id: residue_plddt
  title: Residue confidence
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median pLDDT over the residues in view, and the box shows its quartiles. It answers how confident a typical residue is.
    How to read: a median above 70 means most residues are confidently placed. A long lower box points to disordered or poorly predicted regions.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34791371/
  column: value
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median pLDDT, with its spread

- component: card
  id: confident_share
  title: Confidently placed residues
  description: |-
    The hero number is the percentage of residues at pLDDT 70 or more, and the box shows its spread across structures. It answers how much of the predicted structure is reliable.
    How to read: a high percentage means a mostly confident model. A low one marks hard or disordered targets, so check the per-residue tiles.
    Lines and annotations: 70 is the lower edge of the confident band of AlphaFold DB.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34791371/
  column: confidently_placed
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: share of residues, with its spread
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: residue_bands
  title: Residues by confidence band
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of residues in view, the bars rank the confidence bands by how many residues fall in each, and the line below gives the longest structure. It answers which band dominates.
    How to read: a leading very high or confident band means a reliable model. A leading low or very low band means most of the structure is uncertain.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34791371/
  column: position
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: category
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: residues, by confidence band

- component: figure
  id: plddt_histogram
  title: Residue confidence distribution
  description: |-
    Each bar counts residues in a pLDDT bin, coloured by engine. It answers how confidence is distributed over the residues.
    How to read: a pile near 90 to 100 means a confident model, and a second mass below 50 marks disordered residues. Compare engines to see which one is more decided.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34791371/
  visu_type: histogram
  dict_kwargs:
    x: value
    color: engine
    labels:
      value: pLDDT
      engine: Engine

- component: interactive
  title: Engine
  description: Show the structures of one engine.
  interactive_type: Select
  column_name: engine

- component: interactive
  title: Residue position
  description: Restrict the tiles to a stretch of residues, for example a domain.
  interactive_type: RangeSlider
  column_name: position

- component: table
  title: Residue confidence
  description: |-
    One row per residue with its chain, amino acid, pLDDT and confidence band. Selecting rows highlights the residues on the structure.
    How to read: sort by pLDDT to list the weakest residues.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: position
